repo.description:
### Impact

When rendering notification emails, Discourse converts embedded iframes into links and inlines images from secure uploads. Both were built by inserting post content into HTML strings. A user could craft a post so that the notification emails other users receive for it contained injected HTML attributes, for example to restyle the email or disguise a link.

The iframe case requires the iframe's origin to be allowed by the `allowed_iframes` site setting. The image case requires secure uploads with `secure_uploads_allow_embed_images_in_emails` enabled.

### Patches

The link and image are now built as HTML nodes, and image dimensions must be numeric. Fixed in `2026.11.0-latest`. Fixed release versions will be added after the fix and backports are released.

### Workarounds

Disable `secure_uploads_allow_embed_images_in_emails` to mitigate the image case. For the iframe case, remove unneeded origins from `allowed_iframes`; this disables those embeds in posts.

### References

None.
repo.summary: HTML injection in notification emails via iframe URLs and secure image sizes
